How much of a crowded trade’s demand would remain if momentum stopped?

Funded crowding has support from cash flow, organic spot demand or supply sinks that can persist after momentum fades. Borrowed crowding depends more heavily on leverage and momentum moving through a thin float.

Protocol growth provides durable support for a token only when activity creates demand for it. Fees can fund buybacks and usage can require users to own the token. Without a clear link, revenue and user growth can rise without increasing token demand.

Once the market turns, the recovery depends on whether those sources of demand are still in place.

maybe all of these EF spinouts are a way to do it, but they are also comprised almost 100% of ex-EF people who may require financial and governance incentives to present a different PoV which challenges the historic "ivory tower" perspectives which have dominated Ethereum development and adoption discourse

those perspectives haven't always been bad and often come from well-intentioned places, but they are often overly opinionated, too confident in their own assertions, do not give any regard to real social consensus or likely market dynamics, and prioritize secondary issues with complex second and third order effects which are often not anticipated and detract from efforts to grow scale the network and grow adoption

the alternative is you're going to have a small group of people tell you how the protocol should be run and risks of contentious hard forks

this is the time to organize and actually flex your muscles
